summary.headline: Shalby Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 9.4% to INR295.5 crore and EBITDA 43.1% to INR37.4 crore, with PAT lifted by a lower tax regime.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 9.4% YoY to INR295.5 crore and EBITDA rose to INR37.4 crore (margin 12.7% vs 9.7%). Consolidated PAT swung to INR18.5 crore from a loss of INR12.2 crore, helped by the move to the new 25% tax regime. Full-year revenue grew 4.8% to INR1,168.2 crore, and management attributed the slowdown to Gurugram turbulence, the US-Iran conflict affecting international patients, government payment delays and doctor attrition. Standalone EBITDA was flat YoY at INR37.1 crore, with margin down to 16.1% from 17.7%. MedTech revenue grew about 45% YoY to roughly INR40 crore with EBITDA turning positive for a second straight quarter.

segments.name: Shalby Hospitals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 standalone revenue INR230.4 crore (+7.6% YoY); ARPOB INR42,689 (+2.7%); ALOS 3.81 days vs 3.68; occupied beds 649 (+2.4%), occupancy 48% (50% excluding Shalby International). Payer mix 33% self-pay, 37% insurance, 30% government.

segments.name: Shalby International (Gurugram)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR21.5 crore vs INR22.8 crore a year ago, hit by Middle East conflict; ARPOB INR88,592, ALOS 3.44 days, international patients 47% of its revenue. Group international revenue about INR12.8 crore in Q4 (INR9.1 crore Gurugram, INR3.6 crore other Shalby units). Equity infusion of about INR60 crore raised stake from ~87% to ~91%.

segments.name: Shalby MedTech (implants)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue about INR40 crore with EBITDA of about INR3.7 crore, the second consecutive positive EBITDA quarter; management targets double-digit EBITDA and positive cash flow, not yet reached. Categories are knee (3-4 products) and hip (3 products), with no new categories planned.

guidance_outlook: Implant business targeted at about INR600-650 crore revenue by 2030 with EBITDA above 15%; about INR600-700 crore in five years with double-digit EBITDA (per Deepak Anand).
Hospital and pharma business: management sees sustainable growth of at least 15% CAGR over the long term, with current installed capacity supporting 40-50% upside without significant capex.
Tax rate moves to 25% under the new regime from 35%, described as a recurring benefit to P&L and cash flow.
Management expects FY27 capex to be lower after heavy FY26 spending (about INR160 crore), freeing significant cash flow.
Management expects a strong comeback at Shalby International in April and May 2026 and sees EBITDA breakeven in the short term, but declined to give a timeline.
CGHS rate revision expected to add 7-8% to revenue, with flow-through to other government schemes from Q1-Q2 FY27.
Occupancy in FY27 is likely to be above 50%, per management; Q1 indicators expected and upside from Q2 FY27.
Franchise expansion will slow from the earlier plan of 50 franchisees; the focus shifts to mainstream hospitals and implants.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR160 crore, mainly LINAC bunkers at Surat and Krishna units, plus robotics and oncology investments (PET-CT, radiation).
Oncology bunkers operate at Indore, Jaipur and Naroda; Surat and Krishna are being added.
Two loss-making SOCEs (Rajkot and Lucknow) were closed, which lowers bed count and is expected to improve margins.
Average doctor count rose from about 350 to about 400 at group level in Q4, with new super-specialty hires.
Curexo robotic partnership is moving from pilots to commercial adoption in selected markets.
demand_pricing: Q4 ARPOB at standalone hospitals rose 2.7% to INR42,689, while ALOS was 3.81 days; occupancy was 48% (50% excluding Shalby International).
Gross margin reportedly fell from about 90% to about 85%; management attributed this to new doctor recruitment and costlier oncology drugs, and expects an upside from here without giving a number.
Government business share has risen; receivables from government are slow to collect.
Shalby International's Africa and CIS business (Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Sudan) and new markets offset Middle East weakness.
MedTech is expanding into Vietnam, Malaysia, Nepal, Iraq, Argentina and LatAm, with Myanmar and Vietnam approvals expected shortly.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Shalby International's profitability lagged and when will it turn profitable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said international patients were 60% of Gurugram revenue at healthy margins, hit in Q4 by the US-Iran conflict; April and May showed a strong comeback. Breakeven timing was not given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is debt rising and where is it used?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowings mainly reflect two recent acquisitions (US and Gurugram). Further borrowing is expected to be limited, and debt-to-equity is expected to improve.

qa_highlights.question: Why were operational beds down YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Two EBITDA-negative SOCEs (Rajkot and Lucknow) were closed, lowering the bed count and occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: What tax rate should be modelled for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: 25% under the new regime versus 35% earlier, a recurring benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did top-line growth slow to single digits in FY26 after 15-16% CAGR in FY23-25?
qa_highlights.answer: Gurugram turbulence in Q2-Q3, US-Iran impact on international business, government scheme disruptions, and doctor attrition, now addressed in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall and what level should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to new doctor recruitment and costlier oncology medicines; no target given, with an upside expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 2030 implant revenue and the hospital growth rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Implants INR600-650 crore by 2030 at EBITDA above 15%; hospitals at least 15% CAGR with current capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Will the franchise plan of 50 units proceed?
qa_highlights.answer: Franchising will continue but more selectively, with no specific number set.

risks_watch: International patient flows exposed to the US-Iran/Middle East conflict; Shalby International revenue fell YoY in Q4 and EBITDA breakeven timing is not given.
Gross margin fell to about 85% from about 90%; watch whether the upside management expects shows up.
Debt has risen over four to five years; management says increases will be limited, but no FY27 debt or margin figures were given.
Government receivables take time to recover; the CGHS rate revision (+7-8%) is still pending across schemes.
Doctor attrition at the PK Health unit in Q2-Q3; the stabilisation claim needs confirmation in Q1-Q2 FY27.
Shalby MedTech is still EBITDA-positive only marginally (about 3.7 crore in Q4), with cash flow not yet positive.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on recovery (Q1-Q2 FY27 upside, Gurugram, CGHS revision, MedTech) but evasive on specifics: management declined to give EBITDA margin, debt, breakeven timing or FY27 guidance numbers. Pressed on international and gross margin, answers were qualitative.

growth.why: Management guides to a minimum 15% CAGR for hospitals over the long term, backed by existing capacity giving 40-50% upside without major capex, plus a CGHS rate revision adding 7-8% to revenue from Q1-Q2 FY27; implant revenue target of INR600-650 crore by FY30 is set but not backed by specific new orders or capacity, and FY26 revenue grew only 4.8% with occupancy at 48%.
